Nothing here is drawn to look native.

2 · Genuine glass over colourful content

Apple Photos, one photo zoomed to fill the screen · the controls are the system's own glass
DefaultGenuine · iOS 26.5 Simulator capture
Glass picks up the photo's colour and light.
Increase Contrast onGenuine · iOS 26.5 Simulator capture
Controls become more opaque with stronger edges.
Reduce Transparency onGenuine · iOS 26.5 Simulator capture
Controls become solid (dark in this viewer).

What these show

  • Real glass is adaptive: it changes with the content beneath and with each setting. Our CSS drawing is a fixed recipe.
  • The system handles the settings for native controls; Flutter-drawn glass has to do it itself (section 5).
  • Layout differs: Apple puts Search in its own circle. A native Dottoday tab bar would follow Apple's layout, not exactly E-Phones' four-tab capsule. Whether Search stays inside depends on how the tab is declared: to be tested.
  • Not shown: Mac. A genuine sidebar capture means screenshotting your desktop, which can show personal information, so none was taken. The Mac spike (section 6) produces one.

4 · Integration risks

AreaRiskHow the spike checks it
ScrollingFlutter content must scroll under the native bar: bottom padding has to match the bar's height on every device, and a platform view over a scrolling list can cost framesSpike measures frame times while flinging
TransparencyNative glass must sample the Flutter pixels beneath it. Believed to work because both are in the same layer tree; not yet seen with Dottoday contentSpike screenshots on a device
Hit testingTouches at the edge between the native bar and Flutter; a drag that starts in the list and ends on the bar; long-press select near the barSpike gesture checks
AccessibilityVoiceOver order across two UI systems (bar first or last?); Full Keyboard Access focus; Dynamic Type (native bar scales itself, Flutter scales separately); labels and badges announced onceVoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access pass in the spike
PerformanceGlass sampling plus Flutter raster; platform views on iOS add composition layers; batteryInstruments on the oldest supported iPhone
TestingFlutter golden and widget tests cannot see native views; native chrome needs XCUITest or device screenshotsPlan test coverage before adopting
iPadA native UITabBarController on iPadOS 18+ can show tabs at the top or as a sidebar, which would change the iPad layout (Round 2)Check on the iPad simulator in the spike
MaintenanceNative code in two runners; behaviour changes with each iOS/macOS releaseADR if adopted

5 · Fallbacks

SituationNative-first (B)Flutter approximation (A)
iOS 26 and laterNative: Liquid Glass drawn by iOSFlutter approximation
iOS 16–25 (app minimum is iOS 16)Native: the system's own pre-glass bar, automaticallySame approximation, which would look newer than the OS
Reduce Transparency (iOS, Mac)System makes it opaque (captured above)Flutter cannot read this setting (Flutter 3.47.8 AccessibilityFeatures has no such flag); needs a small native bridge, or the solid look always
Increase ContrastSystem adds contrast (captured above)Flutter reads it on iOS and Android 14+ (highContrast), not on Mac
Mac (app minimum macOS 12)NSVisualEffectView exists on every supported version; the system follows Reduce TransparencyFlutter blur shows only the app's own content, never the desktop
AndroidUnchanged: Material 3, blur on 12+, solid tonal belowSame
WebSolidSolid

6 · Feasibility test plan (not run; needs your go-ahead)

  • Where: a throwaway sample app outside the production code (no change to app/, no new package). If it later moves into the app: a branch from origin/main, an ADR and your approval.
  • Spike 1 · iPhone tab bar (time box 2 days): a Flutter list of 200 task-like rows; variant N1 native UITabBarController hosting the Flutter view; variant N2 a native tab bar in a UiKitView over Flutter. Run on an iOS 26 device, an iOS 18 device or simulator, and the iPad simulator.
  • Checks: glass shows the Flutter rows beneath; frame times while flinging (Instruments, 120 Hz); taps on tabs while the list moves; the Inbox badge and selected tab stay in sync; VoiceOver order and labels; Full Keyboard Access; Dynamic Type to the largest size; Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast; teal tint on the selected tab; memory.
  • Spike 2 · Mac sidebar (time box 1 day): a sample macOS app with NSVisualEffectView (sidebar material) behind a transparent Flutter view, Flutter sidebar rows on top. Checks: vibrancy with two desktop wallpapers, light and dark, resize and full screen, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast, clicks and keyboard focus, frame times.
  • Pass criteria (proposed): no visible dropped frames while scrolling; glass shows the content beneath; VoiceOver and keyboard work end to end; both accessibility settings handled; test coverage plan exists.
  • Output: a short report with genuine device screenshots (yours to review before anything is stored), and a recommendation per element.
